transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-03
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Anya Patel (RelayPoint Head of ML), Marcus Liu (RelayPoint Platform Eng), Priya Nair (RelayPoint Security), Jordan Hayes (RelayPoint Product)

Summary:
Quick intro/launchpad orientation for RelayPoint's pilot. Primary goals: establish network and security intake, agree pilot success metrics (latency/cost/quality), confirm stakeholders and next steps for a 3-week pilot. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs and initial integration plan.

Topics:
- Pilot scope & success criteria
- Network/VPC requirements and data residency
- Security and compliance docs (SOC2, SAML, KMS)
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs; batching/quantization suggestions
- Timeline and immediate actions for pilot kickoff

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for making the time. quick round robin before we dive?
[00:12] Anya Patel: Hi, Anya here. i'll be owning model quality and evals. happy to be on the call.
[00:18] Marcus Liu: Marcus - infra. i'll handle networking and peering.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Priya - security. SOC2 + SSO contact.
[00:26] Jordan Hayes: Jordan - product, will align success metrics to roadmap.
[00:30] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia from Red wood success — i'll be your CSM through the launchpad. (laughs) Red wood.
[00:36] Devon Park: Devon, SE. i'll cover perf, se-up, and any demo bits.
[00:42] Alex Kim: Great. high level, RelayPoint wants to run a 3-week pilot to validate recommendations for answering internal support questions with LLMs. key success: sub-200ms median generation for short answers, under $0.003 per turn, and no PII leakage. does that sound right Anya / Jordan?
[01:05] Anya Patel: yes that's the gist. we have about 1.2M docs and expect about 200 req/s peak for search-assist in week 2 of pilot.
[01:20] Jordan Hayes: timing is also tied to Q3 roadmap. if we see good perf, we'll expand to 5 endpoints.
[01:27] Marcus Liu: Quick Q - are you expecting dedicated GPUs for pilot or hosted?
[01:31] Alex Kim: good call. for pilot we usually suggest hosted because it's faster to spin up, but for throughput and consistent p95 you might prefer a small Dedicated pool. Devon, maybe you can speak to latency tradeoffs?
[01:43] Devon Park: Sure. Hosted is simplest; we can hit your median targets with the curated open model we recommend but p95 variability depends on noisy neighbors unless you choose a dedicated node. for 200 rps steady, i'd recommend starting with a small dedicated pool to avoid throttling and get stable kv cache benefits. quantization moves you to lower mem and lower cost but watch some small quality shifts.
[02:12] Priya Nair: on security, we'll need SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and SSO/SAML for our teams. also KMS integration for key management — does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[02:25] Sofia Alvarez: yes, Private offers KMS/HSM integrations; for Hosted we have encrypted-at-rest and we can discuss bring-your-own-key for Private deployments. i'll drop the security pack after the call.
[02:38] Alex Kim: i'll include the security pack link in follow up — it has SOC2, pen test summaries, and our SAML docs.
[02:45] Anya Patel: great. also, question about data residency — some of our docs are EU-only, can we keep certain routes in eu-west?
[02:54] Devon Park: absolutely; the routing layer supports region pinning. you'll be able to route EU documents to eu regions and keep logs separate. small caveat: cross-region KV cache benefits might be limited.
[03:12] Marcus Liu: network-wise, we'll need guidance for VPC peering and egress rules. we use strict firewalling.
[03:18] Alex Kim: we'll share a network checklist. typical items: outbound TLS 443 to Redwood ingress endpoints, allow inbound only if using private connectors, and list of IP ranges for peering.
[03:32] Marcus Liu: can you provide the IP ranges?
[03:35] Devon Park: yes i'll attach a ranges doc — there's also an option to set up private connect which needs a little coordination.
[03:42] Jordan Hayes: about pilot metrics… how do you capture token-level cost downstream? we need transparency for product ROI.
[03:48] Sofia Alvarez: Console shows token-level cost and per-route breakdowns, plus traces for latency. we'll give you access to the demo org for visibility.
[03:59] Anya Patel: will we be able to run A/B between quantized and fp16 runs?
[04:05] Devon Park: yes, rollouts support canary and A/B; you can pin traffic and compare quality metrics. we also have automatic fallback policies.
[04:16] Alex Kim: (interrupting) ok quick logistics: proposed pilot timeline — week 0 (this week): network and security handoff, week 1: ingest + baseline evals, week 2: perf tuning and dedicated trial if needed, week 3: final evaluation and go/no-go. does that align?
[04:32] Jordan Hayes: that aligns but we may need another week for internal approvals.
[04:36] Priya Nair: approvals plus procurement - we might need an NDA amendment for some datasets.
[04:42] Alex Kim: understood. Sofia, can you help with procurement docs?
[04:46] Sofia Alvarez: yep — i'll coordinate with legal and send a vendor pack.
[04:50] Anya Patel: on evals: we'll provide a gold prompt set and expected outputs. Do you recommend a particular format?
[04:58] Devon Park: JSONL with prompt, response, and rubric columns works best. we'll ingest into our eval harness.
[05:06] Marcus Liu: earlier Devon mentioned kv caching — any special setup?
[05:11] Devon Park: minimal — if you use session-based keys we get prefix caching. for search-assist you'll want to send doc IDs as context and let the runtime manage the KV cache.
[05:24] Jordan Hayes: cost - approximate numbers? we want order of magnitude to plan the procurement.
[05:29] Alex Kim: i'll include a cost estimate inline with the pricing tiers. rough ballpark: hosted for your workload ~ $X per 1k tokens; Dedicated amortized lower per-token but upfront reserve. Devon will send a tailored sheet.
[05:43] Marcus Liu: is there any compliance for air-gapped on prem? we sometimes have marketing requests for strictly air-gapped clients.
[05:50] Sofia Alvarez: Redwood Private has an on-prem package but it's an enterprise engagement; timeline is usually longer. for pilot we recommend hosted or dedicated in your VPC region.
[06:05] Anya Patel: Could we run a perf baseline on a 2k token sequence — just to see p95 under load?
[06:12] Devon Park: yes i'll spin up a quick bench, emulate 200 rps burst for 5 minutes and report med/p95. give me sample prompts and i'll do it after the call.
[06:23] Priya Nair: regarding logs: we need audit logs for token identifiers and redaction — do you redact by default?
[06:32] Sofia Alvarez: logs can be configured; we support configurable retention and can exclude full inputs if required. for sensitive PII, you can use prefix-stripping before sending.
[06:46] Jordan Hayes: any known gotchas with embeddings vs rerank pipelines?
[06:51] Devon Park: embeddings are separate unit costs; if you do hybrid search + rerank, batching is key. we recommend caching embeddings for static docs and only re-embedding changed docs.
[07:05] Alex Kim: ok i'll pivot to next steps in a sec — any other blockers?
[07:10] Anya Patel: one more — SSO: we use Azure AD; how long to set that up?
[07:15] Sofia Alvarez: SAML SSO with Azure AD typically takes 1-2 days once we have the SAML metadata. i'll route you the setup guide.
[07:24] Marcus Liu: about networking again, do you support private endpoints where traffic never traverses public internet?
[07:30] Devon Park: yes, we have Private Connect and VPC Peering options depending on region. Private Connect is preferred when you want no public egress.
[07:42] Jordan Hayes: great. timeline note: we'll aim for pilot kickoff after procurement sign-off, probably 5/11 at the earliest.
[07:50] Alex Kim: noted. Sofia and i will sync with procurement.
[07:55] (brief side conversation)
[08:30] Devon Park: i'll summarize the perf hypothesis: with small Dedicated pool + quantization we expect median below 200ms and p95 under 450ms for your 512-token average. if we need lower p95 we'll recommend resource bump or model variant.
[09:05] Anya Patel: good — we'll add those numbers to our eval rubric.
[09:30] Priya Nair: procurement tends to ask for data processing addendum; do you have a template?
[09:36] Sofia Alvarez: yes, i'll attach our DPA and standard contract artifacts in the follow up.
[09:42] Marcus Liu: any demo mechanics we should know of? do you need sample creds for staging?
[09:47] Alex Kim: we'll give you a staging token with limited scope; we also have demo org access for console exploration.
[10:01] Jordan Hayes: can we do a quick walk through of the console?
[10:05] Devon Park: sure, quick share. (screen share noise) So here is the per-route latency chart, token breakdown, and rollout controls. you can pin traffic to a dev or canary variant and measure quality side-by-side.
[12:10] Anya Patel: looks straightforward — the eval traces will help us map regressions.
[12:25] Jordan Hayes: one last question — escalation path for incidents?
[12:30] Alex Kim: AE -> CSM -> SE. For Dedicated customers we offer 24/7 on-call tiers as an add-on. i'll include SLA details in the pack.
[12:44] Priya Nair: ok thanks. that helps.
[12:48] (longer pause while screen share continues)
[15:00] Alex Kim: circling back — recap of agreed next steps: i'll send runbook, security pack, and pricing; Devon will run perf bench; Marcus will share network details; Priya will send security contact; Sofia will loop in procurement.
[15:18] Jordan Hayes: sounds good. any risks you foresee in the pilot?
[15:22] Devon Park: main risk is underestimated token volume or very spiky traffic causing p95 pain. mitigations: autoscaling policies, burst buffer, and temporary Dedicated burst capacity.
[15:36] Anya Patel: quality risk if quantization changes outputs — we'll keep baseline evals to detect that.
[15:42] Marcus Liu: and security risk if we don't get the SAML set up before users need access.
[15:48] Alex Kim: we'll prioritize SAML and network checklist in the follow up.
[16:00] Sofia Alvarez: ok i'll send calendar invites for the VPC deep-dive and procurement sync; propose 60 minutes each.
[16:08] Marcus Liu: prefer mornings — i'll accept based on that.
[16:12] Alex Kim: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet.
[16:18] Anya Patel: thanks all.
[16:20] (call ends)

Notes on artifacts shared during call:
- Onboarding runbook (link sent in follow-up)
- Security pack (SOC2, DPA template, SAML guide)
- Console demo access
- Perf spreadsheet (to be shared by Devon)

End of transcript.
